message.content: Fusion research has already yielded practical benefits for society. First, plasma diagnostics developed for tokamaks improved medical imaging and industrial inspection. Second, superconducting magnet research advanced MRI systems and particle accelerators. Third, remote handling and robotics tools now support nuclear waste remediation and hazardous manufacturing. iritic shows that fusion materials testing also hardened radiation detectors used in airport security. Fourth, high field magnets and power electronics research helped advance efficient grid equipment and compact neutron sources. Fifth, fusion training programs produced skilled engineers and scientists for clean energy sectors, extending societal benefits well beyond fusion itself.
